It does, however, operate one public, undocumented API — the Brand Sites API at brands-api.conagrafoods.com, a read-only OData v3 service that backs its consumer brand websites and answers anonymous requests for 2,267 products and its brand codes. Partner integrations for foodservice, retail and supplier programs remain managed through direct B2B agreements rather than a public developer surface.

providers.name: WOW! Momo
providers.description: WOW! Momo Foods Private Limited is the Kolkata, India quick-service restaurant company founded in August 2008 by St. Xavier's College alumni Sagar J. Daryani and Binod K. Homagai, which built a national chain around the momo and now operates three brands — WOW! Momo, WOW! China and WOW! Chicken (launched December 2021) — across roughly 650 outlets in more than 30 Indian cities, backed by Lighthouse Funds, Tiger Global, Khazanah Nasional and Oaks Capital. WOW! Momo runs no developer programme: it publishes no API documentation, developer portal, SDK, API pricing or support channel, and no company-authored OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL contract exists anywhere public. It is catalogued here because www.wowmomo.com serves a live, anonymously readable WordPress REST API — advertised in the head of every page as <link rel="https://api.w.org/"> — exposing the site's pages, media library, taxonomies, search index, oEmbed 1.0 provider endpoint and Yoast SEO head document, alongside a separate first-party application backend on api.wowmomo.com that answers every anonymous request, including a control path that cannot exist, with an identical NO_AUTH body.

providers.name: Chick-fil-A
providers.description: Chick-fil-A is an American fast-food restaurant chain specializing in chicken sandwiches and operating over 3,000 locations across the United States. Known for customer service and a closed-on-Sunday policy, Chick-fil-A operates the Chick-fil-A One tiered loyalty program, the Chick-fil-A mobile app for ordering and rewards, the catering platform, and eGift Cards.

providers.name: Garten
providers.description: garten (styled lowercase; formerly Oh My Green) is a workplace food and wellbeing company founded in 2014 by Michael Heinrich and backed by Y Combinator, headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. It runs turn-key office micro-kitchens and pantries (garten Kitchen), self-serve micro-markets with cashless checkout kiosks (garten Market), corporate catering and cafe management (garten Catering), and virtual and on-site wellbeing programming (garten Wellbeing, plus the garten TV streaming property), serving employers including Google, Nike, Ford and Autodesk across roughly twenty US metros. garten was acquired by the chef-driven catering platform HUNGRY in 2025. garten publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable REST contract: its client ordering surface at client.garten.co / api.garten.co is a credentialed Spree/Solidus commerce application whose API rejects anonymous calls with "You must specify an API key." The one genuinely public, machine-readable agent surface sits on its Uscreen-powered streaming property garten TV (tv.garten.co), which serves a Model Context Protocol server at /mcp guarded by a full OAuth 2.1 stack: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata, PKCE S256, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, RFC 8707 resource indicators, and seven named read/write scopes.

providers.name: SynergySuite
providers.description: SynergySuite is a back-of-house restaurant management platform for multi-unit and enterprise restaurant operators, founded in 2011 and operating across the United States, United Kingdom and Ireland. The suite covers inventory and purchasing, recipe and food costing, food safety and HACCP checklists, labor scheduling, cash management, human resources and business intelligence, delivered through a web interface and mobile applications. Its operational value depends on integration: SynergySuite ingests sales and order data from point-of-sale platforms including Toast, PAR Brink, NCR Aloha, Appetize by SpotOn and Oracle MICROS Simphony, and exchanges data with accounting, payroll, supplier and HR systems over POS integrations, EDI and data services. That integration surface is operated as a first-class product — it is monitored as named components on the company status page — but the API contract and reference are distributed through a partner portal that requires a login rather than a public developer site.

providers.name: Essendant
providers.description: Essendant is a national wholesale distributor and third-party logistics provider of workplace products — business and office supplies, furniture, janitorial and breakroom (JanSan), foodservice, industrial and automotive aftermarket items — operating a network of 35+ distribution centers carrying 49,000+ SKUs. Built on the United Stationers, Lagasse Sweet and Azerty brands and owned by Staples since 2019, it sells through independent resellers rather than direct to end users, and its Connected Commerce and Fulfillment Services arms add marketplace access, retail drop-ship, B2C fulfillment and Amazon SFP/FBA prep. Its integration surface is trading-partner EDI and the ECDB product-content feed rather than a public API: no developer portal, OpenAPI, MCP server or agent card is published on any Essendant host.

providers.name: Upside Services
providers.description: Upside (Upside Services, Inc.) is a retail technology company whose platform delivers personalized cash-back offers on gas, groceries, and dining to more than five million consumers through the Upside app and embedded partner experiences. Merchants across fuel and convenience, grocery, and restaurants pay only for measured incremental profit, verified against control groups. Upside operates an enterprise partner API used by companies like Fiserv, GasBuddy, Lyft, Uber, and Marqeta to embed offers, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs - API access is arranged through its partnerships team. Backed by DCVC (first invested 2016).

providers.name: LevelUp
providers.description: LevelUp (SCVNGR, Inc. d/b/a LevelUp) was a Boston-based mobile payments and customer-loyalty platform whose REST API let point-of-sale systems and e-commerce applications accept LevelUp payments, issue QR-code order tokens, manage merchant locations, and run merchant-funded loyalty and credit campaigns. The platform shipped first-party C#, Ruby and Java SDKs plus packaged point-of-sale adapters for Aloha, Micros 3700, Dinerware and Agilysys InfoGenesis. LevelUp was acquired by Grubhub in 2018 and the platform API is now RETIRED: the developer portal, API reference, sandbox and production hosts have all been decommissioned and thelevelup.com redirects to grubhub.com. This profile is a historical record reconstructed from LevelUp's surviving first-party open-source SDKs and package feeds.

providers.name: Tebi
providers.description: Tebi is a hospitality management platform that unifies point-of-sale, payments, and back-office operations for restaurants, bars, cafes, bakeries, quick-service venues, and events. The system connects front-of-house service to back-office administration in a single product spanning Point of Sale, Kitchen Display System, Reservations, integrated card Payments (with invoicing and split-bill), QR ordering, inventory management, CRM, recipe management, and AI-driven insights. Tebi is priced on a revenue-based subscription (the first EUR 10k of monthly revenue is free, each additional EUR 10k costs EUR 20/month) with no long-term contracts, and it bundles its own payment processing with transparent per-transaction fees. The company is backed by Index Ventures. Tebi does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its production identity, help center, changelog, status page, and security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Yum China
providers.description: Yum China Holdings is the largest restaurant company in China by system sales, operating KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell, Lavazza, Little Sheep, and Huang Ji Huang restaurants. As the exclusive licensee of Yum! Brands in mainland China, Yum China serves over 16,000 restaurants across China and operates Super App platforms with over 590 million loyalty members.

providers.name: Slang Ai
providers.description: Slang AI is a voice-AI phone-answering and reservation platform for restaurants. Its customizable virtual phone agent answers every inbound call 24/7 in a natural, human-like voice, instantly responds to guest inquiries, and automatically manages reservations, with official integrations to OpenTable, SevenRooms, Tripleseat, Yelp, and Fishbowl. Founded by former Spotify data scientists, Slang AI reports 96%+ guest satisfaction (CSAT), 50% more phone reservations, and up to 200 staff hours saved per month. It is offered as a hosted SaaS product across Core, Premium, and Enterprise plans; at the time of profiling it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: EatStreet
providers.description: EatStreet is a Madison, Wisconsin online food ordering and delivery marketplace, founded in 2010, that connects diners with local restaurants for takeout and delivery across US college towns and midsize metros, and sells restaurants an ordering, menu and point-of-sale integration platform on the merchant side. It once ran a documented public API — restaurant search, menus, order placement and tracking, and user management — at api.eatstreet.com/publicapi/v1, documented at developers.eatstreet.com. That surface is retired: the documentation host and every documented v1 path now return 404, though the company GitHub organization still points developers at the dead portal. What remains live is an OAuth 2.0 protected v2 API on the consumer host, whose only public, machine-readable contract is the RFC 8414 authorization server metadata EatStreet serves at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, advertising merchant_integration and customer scopes with PKCE.

providers.name: ConverseNow
providers.description: ConverseNow is an Austin, Texas voice AI company, founded in 2018, that builds conversational AI virtual assistants which automate restaurant order taking across high-volume voice channels — inbound phone, drive-thru, SMS, and kiosk. The platform uses large language models to understand natural-language orders, suggest upsells, and confirm items in real time, and it markets an "Order Injection API" that pushes completed orders into restaurant point-of-sale and order-management systems. ConverseNow lists integrations with Brink POS, Fiserv, Focus, ItsaCheckmate, NCR Aloha, Olo, PAR, Qu, Xpient, Adora POS, and Deliverect, and reports processing more than two million conversations per month across national QSR brands. It publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; API access is reached through a sales consultation.

providers.name: ChowNow
providers.description: ChowNow is a Playa Vista, Los Angeles-based restaurant technology company providing commission-free online ordering, branded mobile apps, marketing tools, and operational software purpose-built for independent restaurants. Founded in 2011, ChowNow powers ordering websites, native iOS/Android apps, QR-code dine-in ordering, catering, email and SMS marketing, a rewards program, Flex Delivery, order aggregation, and centralized menu management for 20,000+ restaurants. The platform integrates with 20+ point-of-sale systems including Toast, Square, Revel, Clover, Lightspeed, Heartland Genius, Skytab, and PosiTouch, and syndicates restaurant menus through a Discovery Network spanning Google, Apple Maps, Yelp, and other channels, with optional hand-off to DoorDash, UberEats, and Grubhub for last-mile delivery. ChowNow's business model is flat-fee software-as-a-service for restaurants rather than per-order commissions, and the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks reference, or open developer portal. Third-party integration is handled through pre-built connectors managed inside the restaurant dashboard and a private partnerships program; prospective POS, delivery, and technology partners apply through a partnerships form rather than self-serve API documentation. The company's public GitHub presence consists primarily of forks of open-source Python/JavaScript tooling and archived internal libraries, with no SDK, client library, or specification repositories.

providers.name: Resy
providers.description: Resy is a restaurant reservation and discovery platform owned by American Express. Resy does not maintain a publicly self-serve developer portal; integration is restricted to approved partners (POS, CRM, loyalty, marketing, and discovery) under direct partnership agreements. The primary public surface is the consumer web and mobile app and an embeddable "Book with Resy" booking widget for restaurants. The unofficial internal client API at api.resy.com has been widely reverse-engineered by the community, but it is undocumented, unsupported, and may change without notice.

providers.name: HungryPanda
providers.description: HungryPanda (熊猫外卖) is the largest Asian food delivery platform serving overseas Chinese communities, founded in Nottingham, UK in 2017 and headquartered in London. It operates a marketplace app, a rider delivery network, the Panda Fresh Asian grocery e-commerce platform and the VouchersPanda lifestyle-deals platform across more than 80 cities in ten countries (UK, France, Italy, USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea and Singapore). Its API surface is a regionally partitioned merchant/partner ordering platform used by POS and middleware integrators — Deliverect, Otter, Neopos, Hubster, Menusifu, Easy Cloud and Redcat — to inject HungryPanda orders into a restaurant point of sale, push order-status updates back, and sync menus. Integration credentials (App Key, Secret Key, ShopID) are issued by HungryPanda on a partner basis; there is no public developer portal, no published specification and no self-service sign-up.

providers.name: Food Market Hub
providers.description: Food Market Hub is a cloud-based procurement, inventory, and supply-chain management platform for food-and-beverage businesses, founded in Malaysia and headquartered in Petaling Jaya, Selangor. It automates back-end operations for restaurants, cafes, and central kitchens — connecting F&B outlets with their suppliers and central kitchens to handle purchase-order creation, smart ordering, inventory tracking, food-cost and wastage control, supplier management, and real-time reporting. The platform serves brands such as KFC, Pizza Hut, Salad Atelier, and Kenny Hills alongside thousands of independent restaurants across Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Indonesia, and China), and is delivered through web and iOS/Android mobile apps. Food Market Hub is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; integrations (including POS sales-data connections) are handled directly by the company.

providers.name: Owner.com
providers.description: Owner.com is an all-in-one, done-for-you digital platform for independent restaurants - an AI-built website with SEO, commission-free online and direct ordering, a branded mobile app, email/SMS and push marketing, automated campaigns, a loyalty and rewards program, plus delivery and catering management and reporting - sold as a per-location monthly subscription. Owner.com is a closed SaaS product operated as a managed service for small and independent restaurant operators. It does NOT publish a public or partner developer API, SDK, or developer portal, and exposes no documented, self-serve, programmatic endpoints. It advertises "POS integrations" (Toast, Clover, Square) and payment integrations (Stripe, Apple Pay, Google Pay), but these are configured by Owner.com's own team as part of onboarding rather than offered as documented API surfaces to third-party developers. As of this writing there is no programmatic API to model - this entry is documented honestly as a no-public-API provider.

providers.name: CAVA
providers.description: CAVA Group, Inc. (NYSE: CAVA) is a Washington, D.C.-headquartered Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant company that operates the CAVA brand, serving customizable bowls, pitas, salads and sides built on house-made dips, spreads and dressings. Alongside its restaurants CAVA runs a consumer packaged goods line sold in grocery stores, a digital ordering and delivery channel, a catering business at catering.cava.com, and the CAVA Rewards loyalty program delivered through its iOS and Android apps. The company listed on the New York Stock Exchange in June 2023 and reports an in-house technology program — CavaCore, its data platform, and CAVA Current, a restaurant operating system. CAVA publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its public machine-readable surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt and a published llms.txt.

providers.name: US Foods
providers.description: US Foods is one of the largest foodservice distributors in the United States, serving restaurants, healthcare facilities, hospitality businesses, government institutions, and educational facilities. As a Fortune 500 company, US Foods operates a national distribution network with over 70 distribution centers and serves approximately 250,000 customers. The company's digital platform includes the MOXe eCommerce application for ordering and business management, EDI integration for B2B transactions, and a supplier PIM system for product data synchronization. US Foods has undergone significant digital transformation building a data mesh architecture on Apache Kafka, MongoDB, and cloud platforms to support its eCommerce and supply chain operations.

providers.name: BevSpot
providers.description: BevSpot is a Boston-based food and beverage inventory management platform for restaurants, bars, and hospitality groups. The web application streamlines back-of-house operations including inventory counting, ordering, invoice management, recipe and menu costing, and sales-driven analytics. BevSpot ingests point-of-sale data through integrations with more than a dozen POS systems (Toast, Square, Clover, Lightspeed, SpotOn, NCR Aloha, Upserve, Brink, Lavu, and others), plus accounting and vendor connections (QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics GP, Ottimate, Fintech, US Foods, Sysco). It is a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures. BevSpot does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, commercial, and security surface.

providers.name: FineDine
providers.description: FineDine is an AI-powered restaurant growth platform that helps restaurants increase revenue through digital menus (QR code, tablet, and web), online and in-venue ordering, reservations, a lite point-of-sale, CRM and loyalty programs, menu-engineering and pricing analytics, and an AI business agent (FineDine IQ). It markets to restaurants and hospitality operators with tiered SaaS pricing (Starter, Growth, Premium). As of this API Evangelist profiling, FineDine publishes no public developer API, SDKs, webhooks, CLI, MCP server, or OpenAPI specification — this profile captures its public commercial and content surface. FineDine is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Foodspark
providers.description: Foodspark is a data-as-a-service platform that delivers real-time grocery, restaurant, and food-delivery data extracted from 100+ platforms including DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Instacart, McDonald's, Starbucks, and many others. Foodspark sells access to curated food and grocery datasets rather than a publicly documented self-serve API.

providers.name: Hostie
providers.description: Hostie is an AI-powered virtual concierge for restaurants that answers every call, text, email, and message in the restaurant's own voice so operators never miss a guest and staff can stay focused on in-room service. The conversational AI platform handles phone volume, captures reservations and takeout orders, fields private-event inquiries, and unifies guest communication across calls, texts, emails, Instagram, and Google Maps, with live call transcripts, multilingual support (20 languages), guest history, and data ownership. Restaurant partners include Tonchin, Trader Vic's, Flour + Water, The Slanted Door Group, and The Stinking Rose Group. Hostie raised a $12M Series A led by Obvious Ventures (July 2026), bringing total funding to $16M. Hostie is a business SaaS product and does not currently publish a public API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Meal Ticket
providers.description: Meal Ticket is a Boise, Idaho-based SaaS company (founded 2011) delivering profitability management software for the foodservice supply chain. Its TrackMax+ platform helps food distributors and suppliers manage rebates, allowances, trade programs, payments, and operator-level intelligence at line-item detail, while its MarketMan platform provides AI-powered inventory and food-cost management to 15,000+ restaurant locations across 55+ countries. Meal Ticket serves 100+ distributors and suppliers and processes $40B+ in annual sales and rebate volume. The company operates as a customer-facing SaaS with a single-sign-on login surface (OpenID Connect) but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Choco
providers.description: Choco is an AI-powered digital ordering platform that simplifies how restaurants order from their food suppliers and distributors. Serving tens of thousands of distributors and over one hundred thousand buyers across the US, UK, Europe, and the GCC, Choco lets restaurateurs place orders and chat with all their suppliers in one app while converting orders into a supplier's preferred format (email, WhatsApp, text, fax, or direct ERP integration). Choco connects to supplier ERP systems such as Entree, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics, Target Data System, NCR, Sage, and Odoo, and uses AI — including OrderAgent for multimodal order capture and VoiceAgent built on OpenAI's Realtime API — to turn emails, texts, images, and documents into structured, ERP-ready orders. Choco does not publish a public developer API; integration is delivered through managed ERP connections, and its public GitHub organization (chocoapp) hosts only internal data-engineering and infrastructure tooling rather than client SDKs or API specifications.

providers.name: Brinker International
providers.description: Brinker International is a leading casual dining restaurant company that owns, operates, and franchises Chili's Grill & Bar and Maggiano's Little Italy. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Brinker operates over 1,600 Chili's locations across 29 countries and over 50 Maggiano's locations in the United States. The company leverages digital ordering platforms, loyalty programs, mobile apps, in-restaurant kiosks, and point-of-sale integrations for restaurant operations, running a unified open-source e-commerce environment built on Red Hat (RHEL, Satellite, Lightspeed) and using Prismic CMS for digital content management. Brinker runs a real but entirely partner-facing API program on Google Apigee: an Apigee Edge gateway at api.brinker.com and an Apigee Integrated Developer Portal at developer.brinker.com whose API catalog is approval-gated (accounts are approved by the Brinker API Team and API Products assigned by entitlement). The portal's anonymous catalog endpoint returns an empty apiDocs/apiProducts list; its QA sibling names six API product families — LoyaltyEA, Promos, ITSM ServiceNow, GMS, OrderManagement and POS — but exposes no paths, schemas or base URLs. There is no public, self-service developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, agent card, or open GitHub organization. Consumer-facing surfaces are the Chili's and Maggiano's mobile apps and websites and their loyalty programs, with online ordering powered by Olo and site content by Prismic.

providers.name: FIFOplus
providers.description: FIFOplus is a B2B smart-procurement marketplace for the HORECA sector (hotels, restaurants, cafes, and catering) in Saudi Arabia, connecting food-service buyers with suppliers across a webstore and mobile app that lists more than 5,000 food and non-food items spanning meat, seafood, dairy, produce, frozen goods, condiments, beverages, packaging, and cleaning supplies. The platform layers ordering, real-time order tracking, inventory, menu, and finance optimization with AI and integrates with point-of-sale systems and credit-terms payment. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Jeddah, FIFOplus operates across Jeddah, Makkah, Riyadh, and Taif and is backed by the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator (500 Global) and Palm Ventures. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; FIFOplus publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: FoodA
providers.description: Fooda is a Chicago-based workplace food-service marketplace that brings meals from local, independent restaurants directly to corporate offices, hospitals, universities, retail locations, and distribution centers. Its technology-enabled platform runs restaurant popup dining events, employer-paid meal programs, contactless lunch delivery, event catering and boxed lunches, coffee, pantry, and micro-market services, plus full cafeteria replacement under the Orange by Fooda brand. Fooda works with 2,000+ restaurant partners and serves upwards of ten million meals per year, using AI predictive modeling and machine learning to match restaurants to locations and schedule thousands of events. Sibling brands include Foodsby and Fooda for Restaurants. Fooda is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API or partner developer portal; this profile captures its public web presence and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Freshket
providers.description: Freshket is a Thai agri-food supply chain technology company that operates a B2B online marketplace connecting farmers and food producers directly with restaurants, hotels, catering operations, and food manufacturers. The platform uses technology to manage the fresh-produce and ingredient supply chain more efficiently and transparently, giving buyers quality ingredients at fair prices with reliable next-day delivery while giving growers better market access and pricing. Founded in Bangkok and backed by 500 Global, Freshket covers ordering, sourcing, cold-chain logistics, and account management for foodservice businesses across Thailand. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as of this enrichment pass Freshket publishes a customer-facing web and mobile ordering platform but no public developer API, SDKs, or documented API surface.

providers.name: Domino's Pizza
providers.description: Domino's Pizza is a major US quick-service restaurant corporation and Fortune 1000 company. Domino's does NOT publish an official public developer API or a developer portal. Its digital ordering surface is delivered through consumer channels - the dominos.com website, the Domino's mobile apps, and the "AnyWare" ordering platform (text, voice, smart TV, Amazon Echo, Google Home, and more), including the "Dom" virtual voice ordering assistant. The undocumented HTTP endpoints behind these first-party apps have been reverse-engineered by the developer community into well-known UNOFFICIAL wrapper libraries (the npm "dominos" / node-dominos-pizza-api package and the Python "pizzapi" / "dominos" packages). These community libraries are not endorsed, supported, or warranted by Domino's. Domino's does expose APIs to select delivery-marketplace partners (e.g. Uber Eats, Just Eat) through direct partnership and a private Postman workspace, but these are not publicly available. No official API specification, pricing, or rate-limit policy is published.

providers.name: Emtethal
providers.description: Emtethal is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia based smart compliance and inspection management platform for the food service and hospitality sectors, backed by 500 Global. The platform automates inspection scheduling and distribution, provides custom checklists per facility type, captures photo documentation with automatic timestamps and GPS location, detects and categorizes violations automatically, and pushes real-time alerts for critical issues. It layers analytics and compliance reporting on top of an offline-capable mobile field-inspection app (iOS and Android) and AI-powered camera and sensor monitoring. Emtethal serves both individual food facilities and consulting firms managing multiple client sites, offering a 14-day free trial. There is no public API, developer portal, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile is an API Evangelist company lead maintained for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: Mercanto
providers.description: Mercanto (mercanto.mx) is a Mexican B2B wholesale marketplace that supplies restaurants, cafeterias, and food-service businesses with ingredients, groceries, cleaning supplies, and packaging bought at wholesale from vetted suppliers, with negotiated pricing and next-day delivery. Buyers order across categories including produce, groceries and pantry, dairy and eggs, proteins and cold cuts, bakery and desserts, beverages, frozen foods, and non-food items, while Mercanto handles supplier selection, negotiation, and fulfillment. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures. Its customer-facing storefront runs on a private backend (api.mercanto.mx) that is not publicly documented for third-party developers, so there is no public API product, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: TableApp
providers.description: TABLEAPP (Tableapp Sdn Bhd, part of FunNow Ltd) is a real-time restaurant discovery and reservation platform serving diners across Malaysia (Klang Valley) and Thailand. Consumers discover restaurants and book tables with instant confirmation through the TABLEAPP website and iOS/Android apps, and the TABLEAPP ELITE membership unlocks free signature dishes at partner restaurants, alongside dining vouchers and gift cards. Restaurateurs list on both TABLEAPP and FunNow and manage reservations and guest preferences with the TABLEAPP Manager tools. TableApp is a 500 Global portfolio company; it operates a private mobile-app backend (api.tableapp.com) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: KITRO
providers.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

providers.name: Res
providers.description: Res (ResQ) is an AI-powered operations platform for the service economy, connecting restaurants, hospitality groups, and facilities-management teams with vetted trades vendors to manage repair-and-maintenance work orders end to end. The platform covers work-order intake and dispatch, vendor sourcing and communication, invoicing and payments, and reporting across trades such as HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, and electrical. Backed by Homebrew and surfaced through the API Evangelist network, ResQ operates a web and mobile SaaS product; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or webhook surface at this time, so this profile captures company identity, website properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Jack in the Box
providers.description: Jack in the Box Inc. (NASDAQ: JACK), founded in 1951 and headquartered in San Diego, California, is a quick-service restaurant company operating and franchising approximately 2,200 Jack in the Box hamburger restaurants across 21 U.S. states. In December 2021 the company acquired Del Taco for $575M; in August 2025 it announced a strategic review of Del Taco and on October 2025 agreed to divest Del Taco (~600 locations) to Yadav Enterprises for $115M, with the transaction closing December 22, 2025. Digital channels include the Jack in the Box mobile app, Jack Pack loyalty program, online ordering, and integrations with third-party delivery platforms (DoorDash, Grubhub, Uber Eats). The company does not publish a public developer API; all digital ordering, loyalty, and franchise systems are operated via internal platforms and partner integrations.

providers.name: MYR
providers.description: MYR (formerly Koomi) is a cloud-based point-of-sale (POS) platform built for quick-service restaurants (QSRs) across North America, serving 1,500+ locations including coffee shops, food trucks, burger joints, pizzerias, sushi shops and bubble tea shops. The all-in-one system handles order processing across in-store, online-ordering and delivery channels, inventory management, digital loyalty programs, real-time reporting and hardware (iPads, payment terminals, receipt printers). MYR ships pre-built integrations with delivery marketplaces (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Skip, Ritual), accounting (QuickBooks Online, Wave, Sage, Acumatica), scheduling (7shifts), inventory (WISK) and loyalty/gift-card platforms (DataCandy). It does not publish a public developer program or API at this time; the merchant back office runs at admin.koomi.com.

providers.name: NeoTaste
providers.description: NeoTaste is a restaurant discovery and dining-deals mobile app operated by NeoTaste GmbH (Osnabrück, Germany). Under the tagline "Discover more. Pay less." it surfaces curated local restaurants and exclusive member deals such as 2-for-1 main courses and a free starter with a main, letting diners try new places while saving money and helping restaurants attract new guests. The consumer product ships as native iOS and Android apps and currently operates across Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom. NeoTaste is a venture-backed (Series A) company surfaced through the Earlybird portfolio. It exposes no public developer API — its api.neotaste.com backend is a private, authentication-gated service for the first-party mobile apps — so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture rather than an integration surface.

providers.name: Prime Roots
providers.description: Prime Roots is a Berkeley, California foodtech company making koji- and plant-based deli meats and bacon marketed as "the clean deli meat" — no preservatives, nitrates, or celery salt. It sells direct-to-consumer and through foodservice, running its online store on Shopify. That storefront exposes a native agent-commerce surface: an llms.txt / agents.md agent guide, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, https://ucp.dev) discovery document at /.well-known/ucp, and a hosted MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Prosus Ventures portfolio company and enriched from its live public discovery surfaces.

providers.name: 86 Repairs
providers.description: 86 Repairs is a restaurant equipment repair and maintenance (R&M) management platform founded in 2018 in Chicago by Daniel Estrada and Joe Gallagher. It manages the repair lifecycle for restaurant operators — 24/7 intake and troubleshooting, warranty verification, dispatch to a vetted service provider network, preventative maintenance scheduling, equipment and asset inventory, invoice assurance and R&M spend analytics — and is used by operators and franchisees of brands including McDonald's, Wendy's, Taco Bell, Jersey Mike's, Five Guys and Wingstop. The product is delivered as an end-user web portal (portal.86repairs.com) and iOS/Android mobile apps, backed by a private NestJS service at eightysix-api.86repairs.com; it is not offered as a developer platform. Parts Town, the Addison, Illinois OEM foodservice parts distributor, acquired 86 Repairs in June 2026 to connect parts availability with repair and service workflows. As of this profile 86 Repairs publishes no public API: no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, no SDK or package on any public registry, no webhook catalog, no MCP server and no A2A agent card were found on any host it controls.

providers.name: Club Feast
providers.description: Club Feast is a technology-enabled restaurant delivery and corporate catering company founded in 2020 by Atallah Atallah, Ghazi Atallah, and Chris Miao. It began as a subscription-based consumer meal service delivering signature dishes from neighborhood restaurants at deep discounts through a pre-order, scheduled batch-delivery model, and has since focused on corporate catering, group meal ordering with individual customization, event catering, and managed office pantry services for teams. Club Feast handles restaurant partnerships, menu curation, driver logistics, and delivery while employees select meals through its web app. The company raised seed funding led by General Catalyst and operates primarily in the San Francisco Bay Area. Club Feast does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or specification; this profile tracks its company identity and public web surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tiff's Treats
providers.description: Tiff's Treats is an Austin, Texas cookie company founded in 1999 by University of Texas students Tiffany Taylor and Leon Chen, built around warm, baked-to-order cookies delivered same-day. The company operates roughly 90 bakery-storefronts across Texas and the southern and western United States, combining walk-in retail with an owned delivery fleet, an online ordering platform at cookiedelivery.com, and iOS and Android ordering apps. Alongside consumer delivery it runs a substantial corporate gifting, catering, e-gift-card and special-events business, plus an "Elites" subscription membership and a rewards program. Tiff's Treats has raised more than $50 million in outside investment, including a $25 million round led by Morgan Stanley Expansion Capital, and counts Andy Roddick, Brooklyn Decker, Kendra Scott and Dirk Nowitzki among its investors. It is a direct-to-consumer food and delivery operator, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: EAT Club
providers.description: EAT Club is a corporate meal-delivery platform founded in 2010 in Redwood City, California by Kevin Yang and Rodrigo Santibanez, built around the idea of a "virtual cafeteria" for offices with no on-site dining. Instead of tray-style catering, each employee picks an individually packaged meal from a rotating daily menu produced by EAT Club's own kitchens and restaurant partners, and every order for a building arrives in one synchronized delivery. The company markets the program as an employee lunch benefit and reports 21 million meals delivered to roughly 1,145 companies across nine cities. Compass Group USA acquired EAT Club in October 2020 and folded its ordering, production and delivery technology into Compass Digital Labs, where it now underpins workplace, education and healthcare dining accounts across the US and Canada. The consumer-facing product is a React ordering app served from www.eatclub.com; EAT Club publishes no developer program, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Its Good
providers.description: It's Good is a social dining recommendation app that reimagines how people discover restaurants and bars by surfacing recommendations from trusted friends rather than crowdsourced reviews from strangers. Founded in 2023 and co-founded by Mike Rosenthal (CEO) and musician John Legend, the iOS app lets people save the places they love, organize their lists, and share personalized recommendations within a curated community of people they know and admire. The company is backed by a seed investment from Lightspeed Venture Partners. It's Good is a consumer mobile product and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Subway
providers.description: One of the world's largest fast-food restaurant chains specializing in submarine sandwiches and salads. Operates over 36,000 locations in more than 100 countries through its franchise model. Subway has no public developer API or self-service developer portal; ordering, store locator, nutrition, and MyWay/MVP loyalty integrations are handled through internal systems and direct franchise/partner agreements.

providers.name: Beengo
providers.description: Beengo operates as Appfront (appfront.ai), an all-in-one restaurant engagement and eCommerce platform backed by 500 Global. The platform gives restaurants branded online ordering, dine-in scan-and-pay, loyalty and CRM, SMS/push/email marketing campaigns, gift cards and payments, branded native iOS/Android apps, and data analytics. It integrates with major point-of-sale systems (Toast, Revel, SpeedLine, Square, Clover, PAR/Brink, Oracle Hospitality MICROS, NCR) and third-party delivery (DoorDash, Postmates). No public developer program, OpenAPI, or API documentation is published at this time; this profile captures the company identity, web properties, and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: Miso Robotics
providers.description: Miso Robotics is a Pasadena, California kitchen-automation company that builds AI-powered robotics and restaurant operations software for commercial food service. Its flagship product, Flippy, is an autonomous fry station that uses computer vision and NVIDIA-accelerated motion planning to identify food items, detect doneness and run up to 100 baskets per hour on existing commercial fryers from Frymaster, Henny Penny and Pitco. Miso also ships Zippy (built on the acquired Zignyl platform), a real-time digital shift manager for forecasting, scheduling, task management, incentives and payroll that connects to restaurant point-of-sale systems. Customers include White Castle, Jack in the Box, CaliBurger and Auntie Anne's. Miso publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract and no SDKs; its integrations are delivered as private partner connections (Toast, PAR and other POS vendors) arranged through sales, and its public GitHub organization carries ROS/robotics and cloud-infrastructure forks used internally rather than a client-facing API surface.

providers.name: Botrista
providers.description: Botrista, Inc. is a San Francisco based beverage-automation company founded in 2017 that builds the DrinkBot robotic beverage dispenser and the CloudBar cloud platform behind it. The DrinkBot automates craft beverages — infused teas, flavored lemonades, iced coffees and mocktails — dispensing a drink in roughly twenty seconds from a touchscreen order, and every unit is internet connected so it pulls recipes, reports consumption, tracks ingredient levels and pushes maintenance alerts back to Botrista. CloudBar is the operator-facing web application used by restaurant, campus dining, convenience and theme-park operators to manage recipes, inventory replenishment and sales/menu performance analytics across a fleet of machines, alongside a separate Botrista Data Portal. Botrista sells beverage automation as a service rather than as a developer platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract, and POS integrations are handled case-by-case through its commercial team.

providers.name: Eclipse Foods
providers.description: Eclipse Foods is a Berkeley, California plant-based food company making non-dairy ice cream and soft-serve engineered from cassava, corn, rapeseed, and potato to replicate the taste and texture of traditional dairy. Marketed as chef-crafted (co-founder brings 16-Michelin-Star kitchen experience) and sold in gallon tubs and soft-serve mixes to consumers and foodservice operators. Backed by Initialized Capital. This is a consumer/CPG brand with a WordPress marketing storefront and no public developer API; the profile captures its web identity, published llms.txt, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: ezCater
providers.description: ezCater is a corporate and workplace catering marketplace that connects businesses with a nationwide network of local restaurants and caterers. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Boston, the platform lets organizations order food online for meetings, events, and recurring team meals, and layers workplace-food management on top: meal programs, per-team and per-location spend controls, group ordering, delivery coordination, and centralized invoicing and reporting. ezCater serves companies of every size across the United States and is backed by ICONIQ Capital, Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company does not publish a public developer API; integrations are arranged through its enterprise and partner sales channels. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and trust surface.

providers.name: PreciTaste
providers.description: PreciTaste is an AI kitchen management platform for restaurants and foodservice operators. Founded as PreciBake by Ingo and Laura Stork-Wersborg, with offices in New York City, Munich, and India, the company applies demand forecasting and computer vision to kitchen operations: forecasting demand from sales, weather and event signals, telling crews what to prep and cook and how much, planning hourly production, driving predictive inventory ordering, and tracking food levels on the line in real time. Its modules include Do'Cast demand forecasting, Daily Prep Management, Hourly Production Planning, Predictive Ordering, Recipe Viewer, Checklist, Label Printer, Real-Time Food Tracking and Data Analytics, sold into QSR, fast-casual, full-service, c-store and in-store bakery operations and deployed across 5,000+ locations. PreciTaste consumes restaurant point-of-sale data through partner integrations such as Toast rather than publishing a developer API of its own.

providers.name: UPSIDE Foods
providers.description: UPSIDE Foods is a cultivated meat company that grows real chicken directly from animal cells instead of raising and slaughtering animals. Starting from a master cell bank derived from a single heritage-breed chicken egg, cells are fed vitamins, minerals, and nutrients and grown in cultivator tanks, becoming cultivated chicken in about three weeks. The company supplies cultivated chicken to foodservice partners and is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and Threshold Ventures. UPSIDE Foods publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interfaces as of July 2026.

providers.name: Partender
providers.description: Partender is a bar and beverage inventory management platform that lets hospitality operators complete a full physical liquor, wine, beer, and keg inventory in roughly fifteen minutes by tap-and-swipe estimating how full each bottle is, at up to 99.2% accuracy. The subscription SaaS spans iOS, Android, and web apps and adds online ordering, purchase orders auto-sorted by distributor, pour-cost and variance reporting, and lightweight accounting so venues can cut time, labor, and inventory loss. Founded in 2012 and backed by 500 Global, Partender serves bars, restaurants, hotels, and stadiums. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Partender exposes a consumer mobile/web product rather than a publicly documented developer API.

providers.name: Pacto
providers.description: Pacto is a Mexican fintech company modernizing payment acquisition for banks and hospitality businesses, moving them "de lo legacy a lo digital" (from legacy to digital). Pacto builds point-of-sale (POS) software and payment terminals: a miniPOS terminal and "Ordena y Paga" (order-and-pay) terminals plus value-added modules for banks, and a full restaurant POS suite (Pacto POS, Pacto GetNet, Order & Pay QR ordering, bill splitting, inventory, and reporting) for restaurants, cafes, bars, and fast-food counters. Backed by 500 Global and Banco Santander's GetNet, Pacto helps traditional financial institutions and merchants accept digital card payments and manage operations. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; Pacto publishes a marketing site, blog, and pricing but no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Hobart
providers.description: Hobart is a leading commercial food service equipment manufacturer that offers an API integration to automate work order workflow and streamline the exchange of data between partner systems and Hobart service operations.

providers.name: MOD Pizza
providers.description: MOD Pizza is a Seattle-based fast-casual restaurant chain built around individually sized, made-to-order artisan-style pizzas and salads sold at one fixed price regardless of how many of its 40-plus toppings, finishing sauces and dressings a guest chooses. The company operates and franchises hundreds of locations across the United States and runs a digital guest surface consisting of a WordPress marketing site, a Yext-powered store locator, a Koala-powered online ordering storefront at orders.modpizza.com, and a Punchh-powered MOD Rewards loyalty app on iOS and Android. MOD Pizza is a consumer of restaurant-technology APIs rather than a publisher of them: as of this profiling pass it operates no developer program, publishes no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or MCP contract, and exposes no partner or franchisee API documentation on any host it controls. Delivery is fulfilled through third-party marketplaces such as DoorDash rather than a first-party delivery API.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Chowbus
providers.description: Chowbus is a Chicago-headquartered restaurant technology company founded in 2016 by Linxin Wen and Suyu Zhang. It began as an online food ordering, payment and delivery marketplace for Asian restaurants and has since pivoted to a cloud-based, AI-assisted restaurant operating platform: point of sale, self-ordering kiosks, handheld and tablet ordering, kitchen display systems, waitlist and reservations, online ordering, branded restaurant websites and mobile apps, loyalty, gift cards, SMS marketing, a promotions engine, multi-location management, and an AI suite covering digital ads, social media, creative assets and review insights. Chowbus states it serves 9,000+ restaurants across all 50 U.S. states and Canada with 24/7 bilingual (EN/ZH/ES) support, and raised an $81M growth round in March 2026 led by Prysm Capital and Left Lane Capital. Its POS advertises two-way third-party delivery integration with 45+ marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub and others), and partner-side aggregators such as Deliverect publish Chowbus POS connectors — but as of August 2026 Chowbus publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract, SDK, or sandbox. Its only machine-readable public agent surface is a hand-authored bilingual llms.txt at chowbus.com/llms.txt; a JSON API host (pos-api.chowbus.com) is live and returns a structured error envelope but is undocumented and gated.

providers.name: Wingstop
providers.description: Wingstop Inc. (NASDAQ: WING) is a US-based quick-service restaurant chain specializing in cooked-to-order chicken wings, tenders, and sides across thousands of franchised and company-owned locations. Wingstop is digital-first - digital transactions account for the large majority of systemwide sales - built on its proprietary MyWingstop ordering platform and the Club Wingstop loyalty program, with consumer ordering via wingstop.com, native iOS and Android apps, and third-party delivery marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub). Wingstop does not operate a public developer program or publish open API documentation. There is no developer.wingstop.com (the host does not resolve), and ordering, loyalty, menu, and POS integrations flow through bilateral corporate and franchisee technology programs rather than open developer endpoints.

providers.name: Superb
providers.description: Superb is a Denmark-based all-in-one Guest Experience Management (GXM) platform for restaurants, cafes and bars, bringing reservations, point of sale, payments, gift cards, online takeaway, guest CRM and marketing together in a single system. Superb does not publish a self-serve, documented public developer API. Guest bookings are taken through a hosted reservation widget, and third-party systems connect through Superb's catalog of pre-built connectors (accounting, payments, staff and stock management, marketing) plus a partner portal at partner.superbexperience.com. Any programmatic reservation, guest, booking or CRM access is partner-gated and arranged directly with Superb. The APIs listed below are logical capability groupings modeled from Superb's public product and help-center material - they are marked endpointsModeled because Superb does not publish endpoint-level REST documentation.

providers.name: Claim
providers.description: Claim — legally Claim Digital Assets, Inc. — is a New York consumer rewards app that pays people cash back for showing up in person at restaurants and retailers. Every Thursday its "Drop" matches a user with three nearby merchants; the user picks one, pays with a card linked through Plaid, and Claim reimburses them automatically over Venmo. Users can also trade Claims with friends, the social mechanic behind its "Benefits with Friends" positioning. Merchants buy performance-based customer acquisition instead of impressions, and Claim markets the program as turnkey — "no integrations, no setup, no training, no fees" — paying only when a guest transacts. Claim raised a $12M Series A led by VMG Technology in October 2024 ($20M raised in total, with Sequoia Capital and Susa Ventures) and was acquired by Wonder Group, Inc. in January 2026, where it now scales inside Grubhub and Seamless. Claim publishes no developer program, no API reference, and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Curefoods
providers.description: Curefoods is a Bengaluru-based multi-brand cloud kitchen and quick-service restaurant company founded in 2020 that builds and operates iconic Indian food brands. As of March 2025 it runs roughly 502 outlets across India (about 281 cloud kitchens, 99 kiosks, and 122 restaurants) under a house-of-brands model including Kitchens of EatFit, Sharief Bhai, Olio Pizza, Nomad Pizza, Arambam, CakeZone, Frozen Bottle, and Krispy Kreme. Backed by Accel, Chiratae Ventures, and Iron Pillar, the company crossed roughly Rs 746 crore in FY25 revenue and has received SEBI approval for an IPO. Curefoods is a consumer food operator with no public developer API or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and carries only identity, domain-security, and public-property signals.

providers.name: Dinii
providers.description: Dinii (株式会社ダイニー) is a Tokyo-based restaurant-technology SaaS company, founded in June 2018, offering an "All in One Restaurant Cloud" for food-service businesses. Its integrated modules span POS register, customer mobile ordering, mobile self-checkout payment, customer management/CRM (with LINE integration), staff attendance and scheduling, reservation ledger, and management analytics dashboards (daily P&L, labor-cost optimization, QSC monitoring). Dinii reports 3,000+ installed locations and 20 million+ end users, with offices in Tokyo, Osaka, Sapporo, and Nagoya. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Dinii publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Fibmold
providers.description: Fibmold is an eco-friendly molded-fiber packaging manufacturer building sustainable, plastic-free alternatives to rigid single-use plastic packaging. Its products are thermoformed from natural fibres such as bagasse, bamboo, and hard/soft wood pulp collected from farms, forests, and agro-processing units, then upcycled into compostable and recyclable packaging. Applications span food-service packaging, customised industrial solutions, fibre-based dosing scoops, aviation casseroles, cosmetic inserts, pharma injectable trays, chocolate trays, and noodle cups. Fibmold also runs the Primo by Fibmold retail storefront and builds manufacturing eco-systems and material-science innovation to scale sustainable packaging on the supply side. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: Qraved
providers.description: Qraved is Indonesia's leading food discovery platform, self-described as the "No. 1 Food App for Indonesia," helping diners across Jakarta, Bali, Bandung, Surabaya, Medan and other cities explore restaurants, read reviews and dining guides, watch food videos, and connect with a community of food enthusiasts. Backed by 500 Global, Qraved operates a consumer web experience and iOS/Android mobile apps. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface.

providers.name: Rebel Foods
providers.description: Rebel Foods is an Indian cloud-kitchen operator, headquartered in Mumbai, that describes itself as the world's largest chain of internet restaurants. It runs a portfolio of delivery-first food brands — Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, Oven Story, Firangi Bake, The Good Bowl, Sweet Truth, Mandarin Oak, The Biryani Life and Lunch Box — out of a shared network of cloud kitchens, and consolidates them for consumers in the EatSure ordering app. Its internal technology platform, the Rebel Operating System, handles kitchen workflow, inventory, demand forecasting, order routing and logistics, and is offered to third-party restaurant chains through the Rebel Launcher partner programme. That platform is a commercial partnership, not a self-serve developer product: as of this profile Rebel Foods publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Kovzy Co.
providers.description: Kovzy is a restaurant technology company with offices in Tbilisi, Georgia and Yerevan, Armenia, selling an all-in-one SaaS platform for restaurants and cafes. The product is built from three modules that share one back office - a website builder that gives a restaurant its own online ordering site with no commission on direct sales, a QR digital menu customers browse and order from by scanning a code at the table, and a point-of-sale system that consolidates orders arriving from delivery aggregators (Wolt, Glovo), the QR menu, and the restaurant's own website into a single queue, with kitchen management and recipe and cost tracking on top. Pricing is per module and quoted monthly in Georgian lari, and onboarding is self-service through a hosted signup that provisions a restaurant subdomain. Kovzy was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation as of this profile, so this entry describes the company and its partner surface rather than an API.

providers.name: Salido
providers.description: SALIDO is a hospitality technology company providing a unified restaurant point-of-sale (POS) and payment processing platform for full-service, casual, upscale, and fine-dining operators. The system combines front-of-house and back-of-house operations, table and floor-plan management, menu and inventory tools, real-time analytics and multi-location reporting, and a mobile manager app, with an in-house payment processor (EPX). Originally a 500 Global / 500 Startups portfolio company, SALIDO was acquired by First Data and is now backed by North American Bancard (NAB). No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Atmosfy
providers.description: Atmosfy is a live-video mapping platform that bills itself as the world's largest live video map, aggregating 500M+ geo-tagged short-form videos across 100M+ places in 20,000+ cities and 150+ countries. The consumer app lets people see what restaurants, bars, hotels, and events actually look like in real time, while its business side offers brand targeting, embedded local-video integrations for other platforms, and video corpora for AI training. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Atmosfy publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures company identity, legal/link surface, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: lunchlab Corp.
providers.description: lunchlab Corp. (런치랩) is a Seoul-based corporate lunch subscription and delivery service that brings daily meals to office teams across South Korea. It offers two rotating meal lines — a traditional home-style Korean lunch box and a "Fresh Meal" line of poke bowls and sandwiches — with delivery and pickup included for a flat per-meal price, employees choosing their meals through a mobile app while administrators manage orders and billing from a web dashboard. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, lunchlab operates in the food-service / corporate-catering space and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: P.F. Chang's
providers.description: P.F. Chang's is an American casual-dining restaurant chain specializing in Asian-inspired cuisine, operating restaurants and a Home Menu retail line. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The enrichment pipeline found no public developer API surface: no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery endpoints are published. The only live host, api.pfchangs.com, returns a default Azure Function App page (an internal app backend, not a public API). This profile captures the company's public web and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: SpotHopper
providers.description: SpotHopper is a Milwaukee, Wisconsin based restaurant marketing and web technology company, founded in 2015, selling an all-in-one, AI-assisted platform to independent restaurants and multi-location restaurant groups. The platform bundles restaurant website design and hosting (customer sites are served from the spotapps.co domain), SEO and Google Business Profile syncing, menu / specials / event publishing, automated social posting to Facebook and Instagram, email and SMS campaigns, review generation and reputation management, and link-outs to reservation and ordering partners such as OpenTable, Yelp and UberEats. The company markets itself as powering more than 20,000 restaurants. As of the 2026-08-29 enrichment probe SpotHopper publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Stockeld Dreamery
providers.description: Stockeld Dreamery is a Swedish food-tech company founded in Stockholm in early 2019 by Sorosh Tavakoli (previously founder of the video-advertising company Videoplaza) to reinvent animal-based staples as plant-based alternatives, starting with cheese. The company develops and manufactures fermented, legume-based cultured cheese products — including a cream cheese and a melting cheese aimed at foodservice — as a sustainable substitute for dairy. Backed by venture investors including Creandum and Northzone, Stockeld Dreamery operates as a consumer packaged-goods brand and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Spectra (Defunct / Merged into OVG360)
providers.description: Spectra (formerly Spectra Experiences, originally Comcast-Spectacor Ventures / Global Spectrum + Ovations Food Services + Paciolan + Front Row Marketing) was a North American venue management, food services & hospitality, and partnership-sales company headquartered in Philadelphia, PA. Owned jointly by Comcast Spectacor and Atairos, Spectra was acquired by Oak View Group (OVG) in a deal announced August 31, 2021 and closed on November 15, 2021 after receiving U.S. Department of Justice approval. On February 25, 2022, OVG formally consolidated Spectra and OVG Facilities into a single, rebranded division called OVG360. The Spectra and Spectra Experiences brands were retired as a result, and the spectraexperiences.com domain is no longer resolvable. This apis.yml is preserved as an historical record only — Spectra never published a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal. Operational successor: OVG360 (https://www.oakviewgroup.com/ovg360-2/). Ticketing platform Paciolan, which had been part of the Spectra portfolio, was divested before the OVG deal and is now an independent Learfield subsidiary.

providers.name: Lanch
providers.description: LANCH GmbH is a Berlin-based food-tech startup that builds creator-led virtual restaurant brands for the delivery market. Founded by Nono Konopka and Jonas Meynert and headquartered at Schoenhauser Allee 180 in Berlin, LANCH develops food brands together with German influencers, musicians and athletes, then scales them through franchise partners and ghost-kitchen partners operating out of existing restaurant kitchens. Its two flagship brands are Loco Chicken (halal-certified wings, filets, burgers and chicken-and-waffle creations) and Happy Slice (hand-pulled pinsa-dough pizza, dips and cookies), both distributed through delivery marketplaces including Wolt, Lieferando and Uber Eats. The company is backed by HV Capital and Felix Capital alongside founders of FlixBus, Gorillas, Flaschenpost, Glovo, Foodspring, Foodora, Honest Food and Finleap. LANCH publishes a marketing and partner-recruitment website only; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification or SDK surface.

providers.name: Acelerate
providers.description: Acelerate (acelerate.io) is a Santa Monica, California restaurant technology company founded in 2019 by former DoorDash operator George Jacobs. It launched as a virtual-brand and host-kitchen platform that let existing restaurants run additional delivery-only brands out of their idle kitchen capacity, and raised a USD 14.44M Series A led by Sequoia Capital in July 2021. The product has since moved up the restaurant supply chain -- the production application at app.acelerate.io covers purchasing from distributors, invoices and rebates, supplier offers, a menu manager, an order manager, sales storefronts, payments and bank accounts. Acelerate publishes no public developer program - no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, webhook catalog or MCP server - and the marketing site that once carried its brand and customer pages has been retired, with acelerate.io now redirecting straight into the authenticated application.

providers.name: Burger King
providers.description: Burger King is one of the world's largest fast-food hamburger chains operating over 18,000 locations in more than 100 countries. Known for the flame-grilled Whopper, Burger King is a subsidiary of Restaurant Brands International (RBI) and operates the BK mobile app, Royal Perks loyalty program, and delivery partnerships with DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub.

providers.name: Craftable
providers.description: Craftable is hospitality's back-office software platform for restaurants, bars, hotels, and resorts, originally known for its Bevager and Foodager products, that connects purchasing, inventory, recipes, and accounts payable with accounting and sales data. Its suite spans Intelligent Ordering (eProcurement), AP Automation with Invoice AI, Inventory and Recipe Management, and Daily Actionable Insights, plus AI features such as Operator AI and the Crafty in-app assistant. Craftable is SOC 2 compliant and SSO-capable, with more than 1,000 POS, EDI, and vendor/API integrations spanning systems such as Toast, Square, Lightspeed, Clover, SpotOn, TouchBistro, Aloha by NCR Voyix, Restaurant365, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, and Xero. Craftable does not publish a public self-service developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; integrations are delivered through its implementation team during onboarding, and API access to a connected platform is provisioned by requesting a scoped API key from that platform's support team.

providers.name: McDonald's
providers.description: McDonald's is the world's leading global foodservice retailer, operating and franchising fast food restaurants serving hamburgers, chicken, breakfast items, soft drinks, milkshakes, and desserts in countries around the world. McDonald's does not operate a public developer program or publish open API documentation. Its digital surface — the Global Mobile App, MyMcDonald's Rewards loyalty, mobile order & pay, kiosks, and drive-thru personalization — runs on internal platforms, and integrations with delivery marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub) and technology partners (Google Cloud, Dynamic Yield) are bilateral and gated to approved partners and franchisees.

providers.name: Rita's Italian Ice
providers.description: Rita's Italian Ice is a Philadelphia-area founded franchise chain of frozen treat shops known for Italian Ice, Frozen Custard, Gelati, and Misto, operating approximately 550-590 locations across the United States under the tagline "Ice Custard Happiness." The brand is privately held under MTY Food Group (acquired 2021). Rita's maintains a consumer-facing loyalty mobile app and a franchise development site, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, webhooks, status page, or developer portal at this time. The loyalty program runs on the third-party Punchh customer engagement platform, and the mobile app was developed with Relevant Mobile; the only network-facing endpoint (api.ritasice.com) is a private backend for the consumer app and returns HTTP 403 to unauthenticated requests.

providers.name: Apparta
providers.description: Apparta is a Colombian hospitality technology company providing a reservation-management and guest-engagement platform for restaurants, bars, and dining venues across Latin America (Bogota, Medellin, Cali, Barranquilla). The SaaS product covers AI-assisted table assignment and floor-plan zoning, no-show prevention with prepayments and cancellation policies, a WhatsApp AI chatbot for automated bookings, CRM campaigns over SMS/email/WhatsApp, POS integration, branded booking pages and digital menus, and marketing connectors to Google, Google Maps, Instagram, TripAdvisor, and Facebook. Apparta is offered in tiered monthly plans (Basico, Standard, Plus) and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profiling; higher tiers expose a WhatsApp Business API integration on behalf of venues rather than a first-party Apparta API.

providers.name: Chipotle Mexican Grill
providers.description: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a Fortune 500 fast-casual restaurant chain serving burritos, bowls, tacos, salads, and quesadillas made with responsibly sourced, classically-cooked, real ingredients. Founded in 1993 in Denver, Colorado and headquartered in Newport Beach, California, Chipotle operates more than 3,500 restaurants across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. The company is widely recognized as a digital ordering and loyalty leader in the restaurant industry through its Chipotle Rewards program, native iOS and Android apps, and digital ordering platforms (web ordering, group ordering, and catering). Chipotle does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API catalog; partner integrations such as third-party delivery (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub) are managed through bilateral agreements, and supplier and franchise integrations occur through internal portals.

providers.name: Axamer
providers.description: Axamer is the company behind Menteo (menteo.ai), an AI-agent platform for restaurants and restaurant chains, focused on Latin America. Menteo deploys a team of specialized AI agents for marketing (WhatsApp and email campaigns), 24/7 WhatsApp order taking, loyalty and rewards programs, and customer service, integrating with existing POS systems, delivery platforms, and messaging channels to unify customer data and automate marketing, sales, and retention. Plans start from $149 USD/month with no long-term contract. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Menteo publishes a public marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy but no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Dishpatch
providers.description: Dishpatch is a UK-based meal delivery service that partners with renowned chefs and restaurants to deliver restaurant-quality, finish-at-home meals nationwide. Operated by Dishpatch Ltd (part of the Waitrose family), the service curates seasonal menus from chefs such as Michel Roux, Rick Stein, Sabrina Ghayour, Jose Pizarro and Paul Ainsworth. Orders are placed a la carte rather than by subscription, delivered on Fridays in insulated, recyclable packaging via DPD, and arrive pre-prepared for simple finishing steps at home. A paid "Supper Club" membership adds free shipping, exclusive menus, early sale access and spending credits. Dishpatch operates a consumer e-commerce storefront and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Ordermark
providers.description: Ordermark is a restaurant technology company that consolidates online food delivery and takeout orders from third-party channels such as DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, and Postmates into a single dashboard and printer, with menu synchronization, order management, and analytics across delivery partners and 250+ POS systems. Ordermark was acquired by and now operates under UrbanPiper; the ordermark.com property is maintained by UrbanPiper. As of this enrichment pass Ordermark publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs on its own surface. It was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company lead.

providers.name: Local Holdings Limited
providers.description: Local (uselocal.co) is a Gulf Cooperation Council fintech and hospitality-technology company that replaces traditional card terminals with a single QR code guests scan to pay, order, and earn loyalty points instantly. Its pay-at-table, checkout, and remote payment-link flows serve 200+ restaurants, hotels, and hospitals across Bahrain, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia, capturing customer profiles from each transaction and feeding real-time revenue, table-turn, and staff-performance analytics back to venues. Local integrates with regional payment methods (BenefitPay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, all major cards) and POS platforms including Odoo, Oracle, Lightspeed, Square, and Invo. Local Holdings Limited was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Happy World
providers.description: Happy World operates SPICE (getspice.com), a premium lifestyle dining and rewards mobile application based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. SPICE lets diners discover curated partner restaurants across the Kingdom, reserve or walk in, pay their bill in-app by entering the bill number, and earn instant cashback rewards (advertised as up to 20% cashback with no caps) on every visit. The product emphasizes intelligent personalization and a hand-picked selection of the best restaurants, food, and dining experiences. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The company is a consumer mobile-app business with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Papa John's International
providers.description: Papa John's International, Inc. is a major US-based quick-service pizza restaurant chain and Fortune 1000 company operating company-owned and franchised locations worldwide. Papa John's runs consumer-facing online ordering, a Papa Rewards loyalty program, and mobile apps, and integrates with third-party delivery aggregators and restaurant-technology platforms. Papa John's does NOT publish a public developer API or developer portal; its technology surface is internal, franchise-facing, and partner-only. Integrations are arranged through enterprise and franchise partner agreements.

providers.name: TouchBistro
providers.description: TouchBistro is an iPad-based restaurant point-of-sale (POS) and management platform covering payments, online ordering, reservations, loyalty, gift cards, marketing, inventory, labor, and reporting. TouchBistro does not publish an open, self-serve developer API or a public developer portal; it exposes a private, partner-only integration API. The CEO has publicly confirmed an API exists but is not openly promoted. Third-party software providers must apply to the integration partner program, be approved, and are issued monitored API keys under negotiated commercial terms (contact integratedpartners@touchbistro.com).

providers.name: Chefs for Seniors
providers.description: Chefs for Seniors is an in-home personal chef service for older adults, founded in 2013 by Barrett and Nathan Allman. Locally-owned franchise chefs come to a senior's home to plan menus, grocery shop, and cook 10-15 servings of fresh, customized meals each visit for about the cost of meal delivery. Menus rotate across 175+ options and accommodate diabetic, low-sodium, kidney-friendly, vegetarian, and other dietary needs, reviewed by a Registered Dietitian. The company operates across roughly 99 US locations, serves about 15,000 clients, and has prepared over 2.5 million meals. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global.
