Chefs for Seniors publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store
providers.description: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. is an American chain of restaurants and gift shops with a Southern country theme, offering home-style meals and retail merchandise. Founded in 1969 and headquartered in Lebanon, Tennessee, Cracker Barrel operates roughly 656 restaurant and retail locations across 44 U.S. states. No public API or developer portal is published; the company offers a consumer website, iOS and Android mobile ordering apps, To-Go and catering ordering, gift cards, and the Cracker Barrel Rewards loyalty program for guests.

providers.name: Jamba Juice
providers.description: Jamba (formerly Jamba Juice) is an American quick-service restaurant chain that blends fruit-and-vegetable smoothies, fresh juices, bowls, and boosts. Founded in 1990 in San Luis Obispo, California, it operates hundreds of locations and is owned by GoTo Foods (formerly Focus Brands). The brand runs a consumer website, mobile ordering apps, and a rewards program; it publishes no public developer API. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a trinity-ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Maman
providers.description: Maman is a French-inspired bakery and cafe chain founded in New York City, with locations across the United States and Canada. Maman serves seasonal pastries, coffee, salads, sandwiches and its signature nutty chocolate chip cookie in design-forward spaces, and operates online ordering for pickup and delivery, a nationwide cookie and gift shop, full-service event and corporate catering, private event venues, a loyalty mobile app, and a published cookbook. This API Evangelist profile tracks Maman's public web and commerce properties; the company exposes no first-party developer API surface.

providers.name: Cheetah
providers.description: Cheetah (Cheetah Technologies, with its software platform also marketed as Kimelo) is an AI-enabled, app-based restaurant supply and wholesale ordering marketplace launched in 2015 to bridge the digital gap in foodservice. Its eCommerce platform gives small to medium-sized food distributors and restaurants tools for online ordering, process automation, delivery route optimization, supply chain management, and customer retention, with next-day delivery of daily supplies. In June 2024 the company divested its physical distribution business (Pleasanton, CA) to Palo Alto Foods to focus on commercializing its software platform nationwide. The platform provides digital product catalogs, personalized purchasing insights, integrated payment processing, routing management, and automated inventory tracking, and lets distributors integrate directly with their ERP or inventory management and point-of-sale systems to automate order placement. Cheetah does not appear to publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is offered through direct ERP, inventory, and POS system connections arranged with the company rather than self-service documented endpoints.

providers.name: Blendid
providers.description: Blendid operates fully autonomous robotic smoothie kiosks that prepare chef-created blended beverages from real whole fruits, vegetables, seeds, nuts, and juice with no artificial flavors or added sugar. Each kiosk uses AI and robotics to run without on-site staff, taking mobile-app orders with customization and payment, producing up to eight simultaneous drinks and roughly thirty per hour. Blendid deploys its Blendid M2 platform into retail, colleges and universities, health clubs, and hospitals as a low-labor, low-capex, 24/7 automated food-service offering. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech in the Food & Agritech sector; the company publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Meitre
providers.description: Meitre is the leading online reservations, guest, and revenue management platform for the world's top restaurants, with a strong presence across Latin America. It provides a hardware-agnostic, white-label toolkit that lets restaurants manage reservations, availability, waitlists, and guest relationships from a single centralized system. Meitre's algorithms automatically manage table availability by analyzing the setup of each area of a restaurant and demand for each slot, and can require credit-card guarantees to virtually eliminate no-shows. Restaurants pay a fixed monthly fee (no commission), and Meitre exposes a partner integration API at meitre-api.com plus an MCP server for AI-powered natural-language restaurant booking.

providers.name: Mixt
providers.description: MIXT is a chef-driven fast-casual salad and grain-bowl restaurant chain operating across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles. Founded on sourcing fresh, local, seasonal, and organic ingredients, MIXT prepares its greens, grains, grilled meats, dressings, and drinks in-house and offers customizable salads (80+ ingredients), warm grain bowls, sandwiches, catering, and a rewards loyalty program. MIXT is a Certified B Corporation (since 2018), reflecting a commitment to sustainable sourcing and environmental responsibility. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. MIXT is a consumer restaurant brand and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDKs; online ordering is offered through a hosted ordering surface at order.mixt.com.

providers.name: Bbot
providers.description: Bbot is an order-and-pay solution for the hospitality industry, letting guests scan a QR code to view menus, order, and pay from their phones, including placing orders with a server on the same tab. Bbot was acquired by DoorDash and is now offered as Tableside Order & Pay by DoorDash, serving restaurants, bars, breweries, and hotels with on-premise digital ordering and payment, plus POS integrations such as Toast. Bbot operates owner and admin web portals but does not publish a standalone public or partner-facing developer API or documentation portal, so no API products are listed here.

providers.name: Bassetts Ice Cream
providers.description: Bassetts Ice Cream is a Philadelphia ice cream brand founded in 1861 and self-described as "America's oldest ice cream brand." The company is family-owned across six generations of the Bassett / Strange family, retails out of a single counter at Reading Terminal Market in Center City Philadelphia, and operates a wholesale frozen-dessert distribution business serving restaurants, hotels, country clubs, dipping parlors, supermarkets, and caterers within a 40-mile radius of Philadelphia (with distributor partners in the New York metro and Florida). Bassetts also exports to China (since 2008), South Korea (2017), and Taiwan (2020), and ships pints nationwide via Goldbelly. The corporate office is at 1211 Chestnut Street, Suite 410, Philadelphia, PA. The bassettsicecream.com website is hosted on Wix and exposes no public API, no developer portal, and no machine-readable product catalog.

providers.name: Country Style Cooking
providers.description: Country Style Cooking Restaurant Chain (乡村基, Xiangcunji) is a large Chinese quick-service restaurant group founded on 23 November 1996 in Chongqing by Li Hong and Zhang Xingqiang. The group operates two directly-managed chain brands — Xiangcunji (乡村基) and Mr. Rice (大米先生) — serving Sichuan-style fast food cooked to order in restaurant kitchens under a long-standing "good taste at affordable prices" operating philosophy. The company formerly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CCSC and was, at the time, the only Asia-headquartered restaurant chain listed on the NYSE. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hongshan. Country Style Cooking publishes a Chinese-language corporate website (csc100.com) covering its restaurants, brands, group news, recruiting, and procurement bidding, but it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts — this profile records that verified absence of an API surface.

providers.name: Hangry
providers.description: Hangry is an Indonesian multi-brand virtual restaurant and cloud-kitchen company founded in 2019 and backed by 500 Global. It designs, operates, and delivers a portfolio of consumer food brands - including Moon Chicken, San Gyu, Ayam Koplo, Dari Pada, Wai Thai, Pizza Gang, and Accha - engineered to be tasty, consistent, and affordable for the mass market and sold primarily through third-party food-delivery channels. Hangry operates as a direct-to-consumer food and beverage business rather than an API or developer platform provider; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Science On Call
providers.description: Science On Call provides 24/7 AI-powered technology support built specifically for restaurants. Combining intelligent automation with human experts, the service helps restaurant staff triage and resolve operational technology issues across point-of-sale (POS) systems, kitchen display systems (KDS), loyalty programs, staff scheduling, online ordering, training platforms, phones, internet, and Wi-Fi. Staff reach support anytime via text, email, or phone with no app or login required, and issues are typically resolved in about 25 minutes. Science On Call is a Techstars-backed company; billing is handled through a hosted customer portal. This profile currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or machine- readable specification surface.

providers.name: teaBOT
providers.description: teaBOT is a Toronto-based hardware startup (Y Combinator, Summer 2015) that builds an automated loose-leaf tea-making robot offered to offices, showrooms, and lounges as an amenity-as-a-service. For a flat monthly fee, teams use the companion teaBOT app to explore premium teas and dispense a custom-blended cup in under 30 seconds, which companies such as Google, HubSpot, and McKinsey use as a workplace recruiting and retention perk. Founded by robotics PhD Rehman Merali, teaBOT runs a physical-product and mobile-app business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Revolution Foods
providers.description: Revolution Foods is an Oakland, California food company founded in 2006 by Kristin Groos Richmond and Kirsten Saenz Tobey that manufactures and delivers nutritious, freshly prepared meals to schools and senior communities. It is the largest K-12 school meal vendor in California, serving more than 35 million meals a year across 800+ schools and senior centers, with programs spanning district and charter school food service, after-school and summer meals, senior center dining and homebound delivery. The company has been a Certified B Corporation since 2009 and a Public Benefit Corporation since 2021, and reports a 100% audit pass rate across NSLP, SBP, CACFP, SFSP and Title III compliance. Customers order through Centro, a login-gated web ordering portal; Revolution Foods publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Presto Automation
providers.description: Presto Automation (now operating as Presto Phoenix, Inc.) is a Silicon Valley-based voice AI and automation provider for restaurant drive-thrus and quick-service restaurant (QSR) chains. Its flagship product, Presto Voice, is an AI-driven drive-thru ordering assistant that automates order taking using in-house Natural Language Understanding (NLU) and large language models combined with automated speech recognition (ASR) and text-to-speech (TTS), with optional human-in-the-loop supervision. Presto offers a full spectrum of operating modes (supervised AI, pure AI, agent-led, and unsupervised AI) and has expanded into AI-native phone ordering for QSRs. Presto Voice integrates into existing drive-thru hardware, confirmation boards, headsets, and POS platforms through partnerships with vendors such as Oracle, PAR, and Qu, and draws on AI partnerships with OpenAI and ElevenLabs. Presto does not publish a public or partner-facing developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; integrations are arranged directly with the company through vendor and POS partnerships, so no API products are listed here.

providers.name: Grain
providers.description: Grain is a Singapore-based online restaurant and catering company founded in 2013 that delivers freshly prepared, thoughtfully sourced meals across Singapore. Its products include Meals On Demand (same-day ready-to-eat delivery), wedding catering, event catering, gift cards, and the Grain Savers program, with MUIS Halal and ISO certifications. Grain was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub (500 Global among its early backers). As of this enrichment pass it publishes a consumer web storefront but no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API artifacts, so this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Popmeals
providers.description: Popmeals (Pop Meals, operated by Farm To Fork Sdn Bhd) is a Malaysian food-delivery and cloud-kitchen brand offering popular meals at affordable prices through a central-kitchen model and a network of outlets across Malaysia and Southeast Asia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. This is a consumer brand with a public ordering and support surface but no published developer/API program: domain-security posture was probed live, and no OpenAPI, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal was found.

providers.name: Snackpass
providers.description: Snackpass is an all-in-one marketing, point-of-sale (POS), and payments platform built for quick-service and fast-casual restaurants. It unifies front-of-house and back-of-house operations in one system: cloud POS, integrated card and mobile payments, self-serve kiosks, online and QR/table ordering, a consumer mobile app, kitchen display systems, loyalty and rewards, SMS/marketing automation, and commission-free delivery. Snackpass serves thousands of restaurants from independent boba and coffee shops to national franchises and has facilitated tens of millions of guest transactions. The company is privately held and backed by a16z, Craft Ventures, and General Catalyst. Snackpass does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; third-party ordering and delivery integrations (Uber Eats, DoorDash, GrubHub) are brokered through partners such as Deliverect and GetOrder rather than a documented public API surface.

providers.name: Kitchen United
providers.description: Kitchen United was a Pasadena, California ghost-kitchen operator that built and ran shared commissary kitchens — branded "Kitchen United Mix" — where multiple restaurant brands cooked out of one facility for delivery and pickup, including a chain of in-store food halls operated with Kroger. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others, the company wound down its physical footprint: in late 2023 it announced it would sell or close all remaining units and pivot to licensing its ordering software, and on 2024-03-14 sbe/C3 founder Sam Nazarian acquired its intellectual property and ghost-kitchen assets into a new holding company, Everybody Eats, alongside C3 and Nextbite. Kitchen United never published a public developer API, SDK, CLI or developer portal, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or package-registry artifact exists for it. The kitchenunited.com domain still resolves but now serves a residual WordPress shell whose only remaining page is unrelated SEO spam, so it should not be treated as a live developer surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Xiaomishu (订餐小秘书)
providers.description: Xiaomishu (订餐小秘书, "Dining Little Secretary") is a Shanghai-based restaurant reservation and dining-marketing technology company operating since 2005 via xiaomishu.com and the 021-57575777 booking hotline. Its platforms — 订餐小秘书, 宴位 (Yanwei, an AI-driven dynamic-pricing product for restaurant private rooms), and 高能店长 — let diners book tables and discounted private-room packages at Shanghai restaurants through web, WAP (m.xiaomishu.com / m.57.cn), phone, and WeChat mini-program channels. The company cites strategic investment from Ctrip and SIG and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio lead. It publishes no public developer API, portal, or machine-readable surface; api.xiaomishu.com serves a closed (HTTP 403) backend, and the main site is HTTP-only with a mismatched HTTPS certificate.

providers.name: Allset
providers.description: Allset is a food pickup and rewards platform (now part of SoundHound AI) that lets consumers order ahead from local restaurants and coffee shops for grab-and-go, curbside, or dine-in service while earning up to 15% cash back. Positioned as an alternative to third-party delivery marketplaces, Allset connects diners directly with participating restaurants across 100+ U.S. cities, and also runs Allset for Teams for corporate meal ordering. It is a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) with a restaurant partner program; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Ellis Coffee Company
providers.description: Ellis Coffee Company is a Philadelphia-based wholesale coffee roaster founded in 1854 and now in its fourth generation of family ownership. Ellis supplies coffee, tea, hot chocolate, brewing equipment, and POS materials to restaurants, hotels, resorts, office coffee service (OCS) programs, convenience stores, universities, distributors, and vending operators. Customers place and manage orders through deliver.elliscoffee.com and request brewing equipment service through the OnUpkeep portal. Ellis Coffee Company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, webhook program, SDK, or status page.

providers.name: Graphic Packaging
providers.description: Graphic Packaging International is a Fortune 500 global manufacturer of sustainable, paperboard-based consumer packaging. Products include folding cartons, multipack cartons, foodservice packaging (cups, lids, to-go containers), microwave and ovenable packaging, paperboard canisters, and packaging machinery. Markets served include food, beverage, foodservice, household, personal care, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, pet care, beauty, and e-commerce. No public developer APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: HungryHub
providers.description: HungryHub is a restaurant reservation and dining-deals platform operating primarily in Bangkok, Thailand. It connects diners with fixed-price dining packages — all-you-can-eat buffets, omakase, fine dining, rooftop venues, hotel staycations and cruise dining — from luxury hotels and restaurants, often at significant savings. The consumer marketplace runs on the web and in mobile apps, while a separate business portal gives 2,000+ partner restaurants and hotel chains a booking and package-management dashboard. The company reports serving more than four million customers monthly and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. HungryHub publishes no public developer or partner API; this profile captures its public web, discovery and security surface.

providers.name: PathSpot
providers.description: PathSpot Technologies provides a health-and-safety operating system for restaurants, commercial kitchens, food manufacturers, cafeterias, and hospitality venues. Its flagship HandScanner uses light-based spectroscopy to detect harmful contaminants on employees' hands in about two seconds after washing and drying. Alongside the scanner, PathSpot's SafetySuite bundles real-time temperature monitoring (PowerTemp), digital task management (PowerTasks), and food labeling (PowerLabels), rolling the data up into the SafetySuite Hub dashboard with analytics, automated compliance reporting, email reports, text alerts, and optional API-based data integration. PathSpot markets API integration as a data-delivery feature of SafetySuite but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDKs as of this profile.

providers.name: Chefs' Warehouse
providers.description: The Chefs' Warehouse, Inc. (NASDAQ: CHEF) is a premier distributor of specialty food products to high-end independent restaurants, fine dining establishments, country clubs, hotels, caterers, culinary schools, bakeries, and specialty food stores across North America and the Middle East. The company offers a broad portfolio of artisan, exotic, and signature ingredients spanning center-of-the-plate proteins, specialty dry goods, produce, pastry, cheese and charcuterie, dairy and eggs, oils and vinegars, and kitchen supplies. Customers order through a B2B e-commerce platform (re-platformed to Optimizely B2B in 2021, previously Magento) and companion iOS and Android wholesale-ordering apps built in partnership with Unbound Commerce. As of this profiling, Chefs' Warehouse does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or open-source repositories; its digital surface is a buyer-facing ordering experience rather than a programmatic API. This profile documents the company's public footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Wawa
providers.description: Wawa is a privately held, family-owned convenience store and fuel retail chain headquartered in Pennsylvania. Founded in 1803 as a dairy farm and operating convenience stores since 1964, Wawa runs approximately 1,100 stores across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, Florida, North Carolina, Indiana, and Alabama. The company is a regional fresh-food, beverage, and fuel brand with a strong loyalty program (Wawa Rewards) and a mobile ordering app. Wawa operates an internal API management platform (built with MuleSoft) used to connect to third-party services such as Uber Eats, Grubhub, and DoorDash for delivery, but does not publish a public developer portal or expose public APIs.

providers.name: Aitme
providers.description: Aitme was a Berlin-based deep-tech robotics company that built a platform for automated food preparation, deploying robotic kitchen and canteen systems that cooked and assembled meals autonomously for foodservice and workplace-catering settings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company has since been acquired and exposes no public developer surface: no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or hosted domain could be located during enrichment. This profile is retained as an honest catalog record with no fabricated API artifacts.

providers.name: AllTaster
providers.description: AllTaster Limited (trading as Taster) is a UK-registered, digital-first food-brand creator that imagines and operates virtual and physical restaurant concepts in collaboration with chefs, creators, and franchise partners, distributed largely through third-party delivery apps and its own consumer mobile apps. Its brand portfolio includes Pepe Chicken, Out Fry, La Vie Dirty Burgers, Sheesh!, and others. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, developer portal, or technical documentation, so no API artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived; this profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: Bloomin' Brands
providers.description: Bloomin' Brands, Inc. (NASDAQ: BLMN) is one of the largest casual dining restaurant companies in the world, headquartered in Tampa, Florida and founded in 1988. It owns and operates four restaurant concepts — Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill, and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar — across the United States and internationally (Brazil, South Korea, Hong Kong, and China). The company's consumer technology centers on the Web-based Dine Rewards loyalty program, per-brand mobile apps (iOS/Android) for online ordering, curbside takeaway, delivery, table payment, reservations, and waitlist, and corporate supplier portals (BBI Connect). Bloomin' Brands does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; the apis collection below is intentionally empty.

providers.name: Brightloom
providers.description: Brightloom is a San Francisco customer data and customer intelligence platform for restaurant and retail brands. It began as Eatsa, the automated quinoa-bowl restaurant chain, and rebranded to Brightloom in 2019 when Starbucks licensed select components of its Digital Flywheel customer engagement software to the company, took an equity stake and a board seat alongside a $30M round. The product unifies point-of-sale, loyalty, ecommerce and marketing data into a single customer view, reports on data health, runs AI-driven hyper-segmentation and anomaly detection over that data, and recommends the next campaign and audience a brand should target. Brightloom was sold as an end-user SaaS with prebuilt connectors to common POS, loyalty and marketing platforms rather than as a developer platform, and it published no public API reference, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification. The company now appears defunct: the last dated item on its own press page is December 2022, the entire operating estate it once held TLS certificates for is gone from DNS — api.brightloom.com, api-prd/api-dev, the cgp.brightloom.com application, its auth0-cgp Auth0 tenant, and the status, support and knowledgebase hosts all NXDOMAIN — brightloom.com publishes no MX record, and only the frozen marketing site remains, with its /about/ page defaced by injected search-spam.

providers.name: Caviar
providers.description: Caviar is a premium restaurant food-ordering and delivery marketplace that connects diners with local, higher-end and popular restaurants for on-demand delivery and pickup. Originally launched in 2012 and later owned by Square, Caviar was acquired by DoorDash in 2019 and now operates on DoorDash's logistics and marketplace platform under the trycaviar.com brand. The service focuses on curated restaurant selection, quality-oriented ordering, courier delivery, and catering. Caviar does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and captures whatever public, agent-relevant surface exists.

providers.name: chowbotics
providers.description: Chowbotics was a food-robotics company known for "Sally," a fresh-food and salad vending robot that assembled customized bowls on demand for cafeterias, hospitals, campuses, and grocery locations. The company was acquired by DoorDash in early 2021 and no longer operates as a standalone business; its domain (chowbotics.com) now redirects to DoorDash (get.doordash.com). As of this enrichment pass Chowbotics publishes no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this remains an identity-only record in the API Evangelist network rather than an active API provider profile.

providers.name: Core-Mark Holding
providers.description: Core-Mark Holding Company, a subsidiary of Performance Food Group, is one of the largest broad-line, full-service marketers and distributors of packaged consumer products to the convenience retail industry in North America. The company serves more than 41,000 retail locations across the United States and Canada, supplying tobacco, candy, snacks, beverages, foodservice, and other fast-moving consumer goods. Core-Mark provides retailer technology platforms including Core-Source Portal, Retailer Analytics, Core-Mark Ordering, and Core-Mark Intellisite.

providers.name: Culinarybrands
providers.description: Culinary Brands is an Indian foodservice and beverage operator on a mission to prove that fresh, quality food is possible without compromising on taste. The company builds and runs a portfolio of well-known food and coffee brands across India, including Subway (sandwiches / QSR), Lavazza (coffee), and Fresh & Honest (coffee and vending), with a stated focus on sustainability, diversity and inclusion, governance, and CSR. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the public web presence is a WordPress corporate site with no developer portal, documentation, or product API surface at this time.

providers.name: Dairyqueen
providers.description: Dairy Queen (International Dairy Queen, Inc.) is an American chain of soft-serve ice cream and fast-food restaurants operating thousands of franchised locations worldwide, known for its Blizzard treats, cones, sundaes, and grill menu. A subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway, it reaches consumers through its website, mobile app, and loyalty program. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead; Dairy Queen publishes no public developer API program, so this repo currently carries only a probed domain-security profile and identity metadata.

providers.name: DwellSocial
providers.description: DwellSocial is a Techstars-backed, Chicago-area community food service that brings iconic city restaurants to suburban neighborhoods. Members browse curated restaurant offerings, place group orders for scheduled dates, and meet for a convenient neighborhood pickup to enjoy city-quality meals at home. The service also runs fundraisers for local causes and non-profits, and currently serves suburbs such as Naperville and Elmhurst. DwellSocial operates as a consumer web and mobile application; no public developer API, OpenAPI, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment (dwellsocial.com serves a JavaScript single-page app and api.dwellsocial.com returns the same marketing site rather than a machine API).

providers.name: Eatsii
providers.description: Eatsii is a Jakarta, Indonesia based foodtech startup operating a cloud kitchen platform. It runs a cloud kitchen concept that offers takeaway and delivery alongside dine-in service, and markets cloud kitchen space to F&B operators under a franchise partnership model, positioning itself as helping food and beverage companies run a more efficient kitchen in the food delivery era. The company describes itself as combining a heartfelt touch with data and business strategy, and lists 11-50 employees in Food and Beverage Services. It was surfaced through the 500 Global (500 Durians) portfolio. Eatsii publishes no developer program, public API, or technical documentation, and as of July 2026 its eatsii.com domain does not serve a live website.

providers.name: Food Advisor
providers.description: Food Advisor (FoodAdvisor.my) is a Malaysia-based food discovery application founded in 2014 by Kenny Hew and headquartered in Selangor, Malaysia. The service helps users find dishes and restaurants by searching dish names as keywords alongside locations. It is backed by 500 Global through the 500 Durians Southeast Asia fund. As of this profile the public web presence at foodadvisor.my returns HTTP 404 and no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation could be located for enrichment.

providers.name: Freshmenu
providers.description: FreshMenu is a Bengaluru-based full-stack food-technology company that operates its own cloud kitchens and cooks, packages, and delivers a daily-changing menu of fresh gourmet meals directly to consumers. Unlike aggregator marketplaces, FreshMenu owns the end-to-end experience — from culinary R&D and kitchen operations to its consumer ordering website and mobile apps — serving Bengaluru, Mumbai, and the Delhi/NCR region (New Delhi and Gurgaon). The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. It publishes a consumer ordering experience but no public API or developer program; this profile captures its identity and infrastructure posture for the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Jiumaojiu
providers.description: Jiumaojiu (Jiu Mao Jiu International Holdings, HKEX: 09922) is a Chinese casual-dining restaurant group headquartered in Guangzhou and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since January 2020. Founded roughly three decades ago, it operates 600+ restaurants across mainland China, Southeast Asia and North America under five brands: Jiumaojiu (Shanxi handmade-noodle cuisine), Tai Er (sour cabbage fish, 400+ locations), Song Hot Pot (Chongqing hot pot), Shan Wai Mian (Guizhou sour-soup hot pot) and Chao Na Bian (Chaoshan grilled beef). Backed by IDG Capital. As a consumer food-and-beverage operator it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity lead.

providers.name: Kitch
providers.description: Kitch was a Lisbon, Portugal based restaurant technology company founded in 2019 by Rui Bento and Nuno Rodrigues, both former Uber executives for southern Europe. After starting as a delivery-first "dark kitchen" operator, Kitch pivoted during the 2020 pandemic into a SaaS platform that let restaurants consolidate and manage digital orders arriving from multiple third-party delivery marketplaces — Glovo, Uber Eats, Bolt Food and Just Eat among them — on a single tablet, alongside their own direct-ordering storefront, so operators could keep control of their menus, pricing and customer identity instead of depending on the aggregator apps. Kitch raised roughly EUR 1 million in pre-seed funding led by Seedcamp and Mustard Seed MAZE, followed by a EUR 3.25 million seed round led by Atlantic Food Labs. The company was acquired by Barcelona-based delivery platform Glovo in a deal signed in January 2022 and announced in March 2022, and the standalone Kitch brand has since been retired. Kitch never published a public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or status page was ever published on kitch.io, and none appears in the Internet Archive's record of the domain. The kitch.io domain registration has since lapsed and now resolves to an unrelated third-party gambling site, so no live link is carried in this profile.

providers.name: Local Kitchens
providers.description: Local Kitchens is a restaurant company that operates multi-brand "food hall" locations where a single kitchen prepares menu items from a curated set of local and national restaurant brands for on-demand pickup and delivery, ordered through its consumer website and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, it is a consumer-facing hospitality and food-ordering business. As of this pass it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation — its web presence is a Cloudflare-fronted marketing and ordering site (Google Workspace email, Klaviyo, Twilio, Zoom in its DNS records).

providers.name: MealPal
providers.description: MealPal is a consumer meal subscription service that lets members reserve lunch or dinner from a rotating selection of local restaurants at a discounted, fixed membership price, ordering ahead through its iOS and Android apps to skip the line at pickup. The service is organized around its MealPass lunch/dinner subscription and MealFix offering, alongside a partner program that restaurants join to reach members. MealPal operates as a business-to-consumer mobile application and website and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This record was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nextbite
providers.description: Nextbite is a virtual-restaurant / ghost-kitchen company that operates delivery-only food brands out of existing restaurant kitchens, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It reaches consumers through third-party delivery marketplaces rather than a public developer platform; its sister restaurant-ordering-aggregation product Ordermark has since merged into UrbanPiper (a DoorDash Preferred Integrations Partner). As of this enrichment pass Nextbite publishes only a thin marketing website (nextbite.com, "We Put Food on The Table") and exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: OneKitchen
providers.description: OneKitchen is a Dubai-based cloud/ghost-kitchen enablement startup founded in 2018 that provided chefs, restaurants, and food entrepreneurs with shared kitchen space, equipment, and operating technology to launch delivery-only restaurant brands in about 48 hours at a fraction of traditional restaurant capital cost. It was backed by 500 Global, Chernovetskyi Investment Group, and Savour Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company appears dormant - its primary domain joinonekitchen.com no longer resolves to a live product (it now redirects to a domain-sale parking page) and no public developer portal, API, documentation, or other API surface could be found.

providers.name: Phood Solutions
providers.description: Phood Solutions is a New York City-based food-waste technology company founded in 2015 by Luc Dang and Nick Kruczek. Its computer-vision platform, PhoodX, pairs a countertop scale and camera system with a waste-analytics dashboard to automatically identify, weigh, and categorize discarded food in commercial kitchens, grocery prepared-foods operations, and food-service venues. The platform reports product-level margins, recommends demand-based production volumes, and helps operators cut food waste by up to 50 percent, reduce kitchen labor, and lower food-inventory costs. Phood also offers Phood Lab, custom digital solutions built by its food technologists. The company is backed by Techstars. Phood publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Piestro
providers.description: Piestro was a Los Angeles-area food-robotics company that built a fully enclosed, automated pizza-making vending machine — an unattended kiosk that pressed, sauced, topped, baked, cut and boxed an artisanal pizza in roughly three minutes, sold both as direct-to-consumer placements and as a white-label unit for existing pizza brands. Founded by Massimo Noja De Marco and incubated by Wavemaker Labs (since rebranded Vebu Labs), it raised roughly $11.7M from equity-crowdfunding investors, largely via StartEngine, and piloted units with partners including Capriotti's and 800 Degrees Go. Piestro shut down in January 2025 without shipping a production unit. It is a hardware and food-service company, not a software vendor: it never ran a developer program, and no public API, SDK, webhook, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind was ever published. This profile records that absence rather than inventing a surface.

providers.name: Reserve *
providers.description: Reserve was a restaurant-reservation startup backed by GV and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector portfolio lead. Its domain reserve.com now issues an HTTP 301 redirect to resy.com, the Resy restaurant-reservation platform, indicating the product has been folded into Resy. During enrichment no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation was found for Reserve, and no security.txt, bug bounty, or trust center is published on the domain. The profile is retained as an acquired/redirected consumer-sector lead.

providers.name: Restorando
providers.description: Restorando was a Latin American online restaurant-reservation platform (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, and other markets), originally backed by Emergence Capital and later acquired by TripAdvisor. The Restorando brand has since been absorbed into TheFork: as of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass, restorando.com returns a 301 redirect to thefork.es and the standalone Restorando product no longer exists. It exposes no independent developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable surface to enrich.

providers.name: RVDS Inc.
providers.description: RVDS Inc. is a South Korean food and beverage company that describes itself as growing into Korea's representative Multi-K-Food Brand Operator, building and operating a portfolio of consumer dining brands including Dodo Korea, Butai, and Salad Monster. Based in Cheongju-si, Chungcheongbuk-do, the company is backed by 500 Global. As a consumer food-brand operator it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this profile carries only identity and probed domain-security signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Skipthedishes
providers.description: SkipTheDishes is a Canadian online food-delivery marketplace headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, founded in 2012 and acquired by Just Eat (now Just Eat Takeaway.com) in 2016, under which it operates as the group's Canadian brand. It connects diners with local restaurants and a network of independent couriers for on-demand food delivery and pickup across Canadian cities via its consumer website and mobile apps, and runs a restaurant partner onboarding program and a courier (Skip Network) program. As of this enrichment pass SkipTheDishes publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. The primary domain is served behind Cloudflare bot protection and the partner/partners subdomains are static marketing/onboarding pages, so no OpenAPI, webhook, or SDK surface is available to harvest.

providers.name: Snapfinger
providers.description: Snapfinger was an online and mobile food-ordering platform that let diners browse menus and place takeout and delivery orders across a network of restaurant brands. The snapfinger.com domain now 301-redirects to Tillster, the restaurant-commerce company (ordering, kiosk, loyalty, menu, and data solutions for 40,000+ restaurants), so Snapfinger operates today as a defunct brand absorbed into Tillster. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published under the Snapfinger name. It remains in the API Evangelist network as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio lead pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: Sweetgreen
providers.description: Sweetgreen is a fast-casual restaurant company (NYSE: SG) building healthy, plant-forward food through a network of company-owned locations and its digital ordering platform. It reaches customers primarily via its consumer website and mobile app for pickup, delivery, and its Sweetgreen Rewards loyalty program, and operates automated "Infinite Kitchen" locations. As of this enrichment pass, Sweetgreen publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture only. Backed by D1 Capital and True Ventures.

providers.name: TastyUrban
providers.description: TastyUrban is a Berlin-based virtual restaurant franchise and digital-first food-brand licensing company founded in 2022 by Felix Chrobog, Marc Hansell, and Gerry Pidgeon (alumni of Gorillas, Tier, and Deliveroo). It pursues an asset-light model in which existing restaurants and retail partners license and operate TastyUrban's digital food brands, using otherwise idle kitchen capacity to add revenue without major investment or operational complexity. The company is backed by Earlybird and raised a EUR 1.5M seed round in 2023 and a EUR 6.5M Series A in 2025 (led by IBB Ventures). TastyUrban operates a consumer/partner web presence at tastyurban.com but publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Truffle
providers.description: Truffle is an AI-native restaurant operating system building "the autonomous back of house for restaurants" — one platform to manage an entire restaurant operation more profitably. The company, a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) portfolio company operating at usetruffle.ai, positions its product as an autonomous back-of-house layer that unifies the operational and administrative work that normally sprawls across separate tools. As of this profile Truffle is a very early-stage company presenting a single marketing landing page; it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, CLI, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this API Evangelist profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture and will be re-enriched as a developer surface emerges.

providers.name: ypxfood
providers.description: ypxfood (YPX Cayman) is a Taiwanese quick-service restaurant company specializing in Taiwanese food and snacks, backed by Qiming Venture Partners, LionRock Capital, and Ignition Capital. It is a consumer restaurant and food business with no public developer or API surface; enrichment probes found the corporate website (Cloudflare-fronted, returning 403 to automated clients) and no documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or well-known discovery endpoints. This profile is retained as a network company record.

providers.name: Ritual
providers.description: Ritual is a Toronto-based restaurant order-ahead and "social ordering" platform (ritual.co, founded 2014) that lets consumers pre-order, pay, and skip the line at local restaurants and coffee shops, and lets colleagues pile onto a shared order for group pickup. For restaurants it offers Ritual ONE (online ordering, company/building perk programs, and Ritual for Coffee). Ritual does NOT publish a public or self-serve developer API - there is no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or authentication documentation. Restaurant order injection into point-of-sale systems is handled through partner/POS integrations (documented on partnersupport.ritual.co) and third-party ordering aggregators such as Deliverect, not through a Ritual-published API. Operating status - Ritual continues to operate the consumer app and online-ordering platform, but the business is distressed and in transition - revenue fell from ~US$11M (2021) to ~US$3.9M (H1 2024) with repeated layoffs, and in January 2025 Shopify "acqui-hired" the co-founders (CEO Ray Reddy became Shopify's VP of Retail/POS) and much of the R&D team while a separate process to sell the standalone Ritual business was underway. This entry is a documentation stub with no APIs modeled because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: BentoBox
providers.description: BentoBox is a restaurant marketing and commerce platform, part of Fiserv, that powers restaurant websites, online ordering, takeout and delivery, events, reservations, and digital presence for thousands of hospitality brands. While BentoBox runs a Technology Partners program and connects to 50+ third-party services across POS, reservations, delivery, payments, marketing, and shipping, it does not publish a public self-service developer API or API reference. Integrations are built through partnership rather than open documentation, and prospective technology partners are directed to contact the BentoBox partnerships team to integrate with the platform. As a Fiserv company, payments and commerce flows connect through Clover and Fiserv rails.

providers.name: Splash 360
providers.description: French vendor of point-of-sale and management software for collective catering — company restaurants, school and institutional canteens. The product line covers a smart till, self-service ordering kiosks and kiosk software, Wifi Order, a Kitchen Display System, a back-office management layer, a coin handler, and loyalty through a YouFid integration. NO PUBLIC API SURFACE: the company sells and deploys into catering operators directly, and publishes no developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable contract. That is the absence of a PUBLIC interface, not the absence of APIs — a till, a kiosk and a kitchen display exchanging orders are API-driven by construction, but those interfaces reach customers through deployment and integration work rather than a public developer program.

providers.name: Darden Restaurants
providers.description: Darden Restaurants is the largest full-service restaurant company in the world, owning and operating brands such as Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Yard House, The Capital Grille, Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen, Eddie V's, Seasons 52, Bahama Breeze, Ruth's Chris Steak House, and Chuy's. Darden does not publish a public developer API; consumer-facing ordering and loyalty are exposed only via internal mobile apps and partnerships such as Uber for delivery.

providers.name: Panera Bread
providers.description: Panera Bread is a chain of bakery-cafe fast casual restaurants offering sandwiches, soups, salads, pasta, and bakery items with a focus on clean food and convenience, anchored by the MyPanera loyalty program. Panera operates a private developer portal at developer.cloud.panerabread.com (built on Google Apigee X) that lists an APIs catalog and an OAuth-based authentication guide, but the API reference and OpenAPI specifications are gated behind authentication and are not publicly accessible. No openly documented, self-service public developer API is available at this time; access appears to be limited to partners and authenticated developers.

providers.name: Performance Food Group
providers.description: Performance Food Group is one of the largest foodservice distributors in North America, marketing and distributing food and food-related products to independent and chain restaurants and other institutional customers.

providers.name: Graham Holdings
providers.description: Graham Holdings (NYSE: GHC) is a diversified holding company with operations in education, television broadcasting, digital media, manufacturing, healthcare, automotive, restaurants, and custom framing. Principal subsidiaries include Kaplan (educational services), Graham Media Group and Social News Desk (broadcasting and social media tools), The Slate Group and Foreign Policy (digital publishing), Code3 and City Cast (digital marketing and local news), Hoover Treated Wood Products, Joyce/Dayton, Group Dekko, and Forney (manufacturing), Graham Healthcare Group (home health and hospice), Graham Automotive (dealerships), Clyde's Restaurant Group (including Old Ebbitt Grill), and Framebridge (online custom framing). No public developer APIs have been identified across the portfolio.

providers.name: Cheesecake Factory
providers.description: Profile for Cheesecake Factory in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 876).

providers.name: Texas Roadhouse
providers.description: Profile for Texas Roadhouse in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 829).

providers.name: Pocket Menu
providers.description: Pocket Menu (Pocket Concierge / ポケットコンシェルジュ) is a Japanese fine-dining restaurant reservation and payment service that curates high-quality restaurants and lets diners book and pay for reservations online. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The public surface is a consumer web application (Ruby on Rails / React on Rails) at pocket-concierge.jp with no published developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or .well-known discovery documents detected during enrichment.

providers.name: Textaurant
providers.description: Textaurant was an early SMS-based restaurant waitlist and table-management startup founded around 2010 by Josh Bob in Waltham, Massachusetts, and later surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Its software let a restaurant manage its waiting list from a laptop and text guests when a table opened up, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to pager-based systems from JTECH and OpenTable. The original company is defunct: its primary domain, textaurant.com, now resolves to a parked GoDaddy "for sale" landing page with no product, documentation, or API surface. A separate, unaffiliated live app reusing the name exists at app.textaurant.app (a small Twilio-backed Next.js application served through a personal proxy), but it publishes no public API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer documentation. There is no API to onboard against; this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct provider.

providers.name: BIZZON
providers.description: BIZZON (formerly AgentCASH) was a London-based hospitality and restaurant technology company founded in 2015, offering an end-to-end point-of-sale (POS) and payments platform for the food-and-beverage and hospitality sector. Its suite spanned sales/ordering tools, business intelligence, and fully certified cloud-hosted omnichannel payment technology, letting operators manage online orders, payments, menus, inventory, staff, and loyalty. Backed by Techstars, Mews, and Ascension, BIZZON was acquired by hospitality cloud platform Mews in March 2022 and its product and infrastructure have since been folded into Mews; the former developer surface (developers.bizzon.com), status page, and the agentcash.com domain are no longer live, and the your.bizzon.com portal now redirects to pos.mews.com. This profile is retained as a historical provider/company record. No independent live API or developer surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Cayena
providers.description: Cayena is a Brazilian B2B technology company operating an e-procurement marketplace and embedded-fintech platform for the food-service industry. It connects restaurants, bars, hotels, and other food-service buyers with food, beverage, and supply distributors, streamlining ordering, catalog discovery, and fulfillment while layering in payments and short-term credit (buy-now-pay-later) so operators can purchase supplies and defer payment. Headquartered in Sao Paulo, Cayena is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company lead; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been confirmed for Cayena at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Qlub
providers.description: Qlub is a hospitality payments and digital-menu technology company enabling contactless pay-at-table, order-and-pay, digital menus, secure payment links, a qlub SoftPOS terminal, and the qlub+ rewards program for restaurants, hotels, and hospitality venues. Diners scan a QR code to view the bill, split it, add a tip, and pay from their own phone without downloading an app or creating an account. Qlub operates globally across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, Australia, Brazil, and the United States, and integrates with more than one hundred point-of-sale systems. It is backed by Point Nine. As of this enrichment pass Qlub publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal; technical integrations are delivered through direct POS partnerships.
